passage:
Gurleen hung back by the colony gate while the other kids played. Across the park, Nilesh was laughing with his new cycling gang. Last year the two of them had built a whole mud city behind Block C.
"He doesn't even look at me now," she said.
Papa crouched beside her. "Maybe he's just busy. Want to go and say hello? Only hello."
She walked over, heart thumping, and said, "Hi, Nilesh." He looked surprised, then smiled. "Hi!"
That evening, with Papa's help, she sent a message to Nilesh's mother: "Can Nilesh come for one game of carrom on Sunday?" He came. It wasn't like the mud-city days; they talked about different things now.
At bedtime Papa said, "Some friends are for one season, some for many. The mud city was still real." Gurleen thought about that for a long time.

qa.q: What had Gurleen and Nilesh built together last year?
qa.a: They had built a whole mud city behind Block C.

qa.q: How was Gurleen feeling as she walked across the park?
qa.a: Gurleen was nervous, with her heart thumping, but also hoping Nilesh would still say hello. 😰

qa.q: Which steps did Papa use to help Gurleen, and why did they work?
qa.a: Papa suggested only a hello, then helped invite Nilesh for one carrom game, and explained that friends can change by season; small steps kept it kind without pressure.

qa.q: How might Nilesh feel when Gurleen says hello?
qa.a: Nilesh seemed surprised and then pleased, so he probably hadn't meant to leave Gurleen out; he was just busy with his new cycling gang.

grounding: Shows a parent helping a child greet an old friend, invite him to one game, and accept that friendships can belong to different seasons without being false.

passage:
"Ma, Lakshmi sits with the choir girls now. She didn't even save my place."
"Did you two fight?"
"No. She just... goes with them."
"Hmm. You miss her."
"I don't care."
"Bidisha."
"Okay. I miss her a bit."
"What if tomorrow you just say good morning to her? Nothing else."
"What if she ignores me?"
"Then you'll come home and we'll have jhalmuri together. But I don't think she will."
"..."
"And on Saturday you could ask her here for one game of ludo."
"She might say she has choir."
"Then maybe the Saturday after. Shona, people can be close in one season and less close in another. That doesn't mean your friendship with Lakshmi was fake. Those two years were true."
"Can I make the invitation card myself?"
"Of course you can."

qa.q: Who does Lakshmi sit with now?
qa.a: Lakshmi sits with the choir girls now.

qa.q: What does Bidisha's 'I don't care' suggest Bidisha really feels?
qa.a: It hides that Bidisha misses Lakshmi and feels hurt; a moment later Bidisha admits missing her a bit.

qa.q: What small steps does Ma suggest, and why are they good?
qa.a: Ma suggests just saying good morning, then inviting Lakshmi for one game of ludo; small steps keep the kindness going without forcing the old closeness. 🙂

qa.q: What might Lakshmi be experiencing with the choir girls?
qa.a: Lakshmi is probably enjoying the choir and her new company and may not realise Bidisha feels left out, since they never fought.

grounding: Illustrates a parent guiding a child to greet an old friend, invite her for one game, and see that a changed friendship was still real.

passage:
When Lavanya started playing badminton with the girls from 6B, I stopped talking to her. I thought that was fair, because she had stopped talking to me first.

Amma noticed. She didn't lecture me. She just asked, "Do you miss her?"

I said no. Then I cried.

The next morning Amma walked with me to the school gate and said, "Just say hello. That's all. You don't have to fix anything."

So I did. Lavanya looked surprised, then she said hello back and smiled.

On Saturday Amma helped me invite her to our building's treasure hunt. She came. We had fun, even if it wasn't like before.

Amma said some friends are for one season and some for many, and a season ending doesn't make the good part fake. I think about that when I see Lavanya now.

— Shreya

qa.q: What did Amma ask Shreya after noticing the silence?
qa.a: She asked, "Do you miss her?"

qa.q: How did Shreya really feel when saying no to Amma's question?
qa.a: Shreya was sad and hurt underneath, missing Lavanya, which is why the tears came right after saying no.

qa.q: What small steps did Amma suggest, and why did they work?
qa.a: Just saying hello, and then inviting Lavanya to one treasure hunt; small steps did not demand the old closeness, so Shreya could reconnect without pressure.

qa.q: How might Lavanya have felt when Shreya said hello at the gate?
qa.a: She was probably surprised and relieved, since the silence may have confused her too, and she smiled back.

grounding: Shreya's mother helps her say hello to a drifting friend, invite her to one game, and accept that friendships can change without being false.

passage:
Note to myself, Sunday

Rafiq has been moping since Disha started spending lunch with the robotics kids. He said, "She was never really my friend," and slammed his door.

I didn't argue. At bedtime I asked what he missed most. "Building forts with her," he said.

On Monday I suggested he just say hello to her at the gate, nothing more. He came home and said, "She said hi back. She seemed normal."

Today I helped him invite Disha to fly kites on our terrace. She came for an hour. Rafiq was quiet afterwards but not angry.

I told him that some friends are close in one season and further away in another, and that the forts they built were real. He said, "So it wasn't fake?" I said, "No. It was real."

He went to sleep smiling a little.

— Rafiq's Ammi

qa.q: What did Rafiq say he missed most?
qa.a: Building forts with her.

qa.q: Why did Rafiq say Disha was never really his friend?
qa.a: He was hurt and angry that she now spent lunch with the robotics kids, so he tried to protect himself by saying the friendship was never real.

qa.q: How did Ammi help Rafiq keep kindness through the change?
qa.a: She listened without arguing, then helped with small steps, a hello and one kite afternoon, and told him the friendship was real even if it changes.

qa.q: What is it like for Disha to be invited to the terrace?
qa.a: She is probably pleased to be remembered by an old friend, even though robotics now takes much of her time.

grounding: A mother's note shows her helping Rafiq greet a drifting friend, invite her once, and accept that friendships change with seasons without being false.

passage:
Thursday

Today Papa and I made a plan about Bidisha. Since she joined the drama club she hardly talks to me, and I was going to stop talking to her too.

Papa said, "Try one hello tomorrow. Just one." I said it would be weird. He said maybe, but try.

So I said hello at the water cooler. She said "Hiii Raghav!" like normal. Weird!!

Then Papa said we could invite her to play cricket in the lane on Sunday. I wrote the invite on a card. She said she'd come after drama rehearsal.

Papa also said some friends are close in one season and further in another, like how he doesn't see his school friends much but still loves them. I asked if that means me and Bidisha are finished. He said, "Not finished. Just changing."

I'm keeping the card she drew me in Class 3. 🙂

qa.q: Where did Raghav say hello to Bidisha?
qa.a: At the water cooler.

qa.q: How did Raghav feel before and after saying hello?
qa.a: Before, he felt hurt and a bit stubborn, planning to stop talking; after, he felt surprised and relieved when Bidisha answered like normal.

qa.q: What did Papa do that helped?
qa.a: He suggested one small hello and one invitation to cricket, and explained that friends can be closer or further in different seasons without the friendship being over.

qa.q: How might Bidisha see Raghav's invitation?
qa.a: She may be pleased that Raghav still wants to play, while fitting it around drama rehearsal, which now takes her time.

grounding: Raghav's diary shows his father helping him say hello, invite a changing friend to one game, and accept friendships can shift without being lost.

passage:
In the village of Kumbhalgarh, Pranav's Papa found him sitting by the well, throwing pebbles.

"Elizabeth doesn't play with me anymore," Pranav said. "She plays with the big kids at the church now."

Papa sat down beside him. "Do you miss her?"

Pranav nodded.

"Maybe you can just say hello tomorrow. And ask her to play marbles once. Just once."

"What if she says no?"

"Then she says no, and you'll still have the good days you had. Those were real, beta. Friends sometimes change, like seasons."

The next evening Pranav walked to the church steps. "Elizabeth, want to play marbles?"

She hesitated, then grinned. "One game."

They played two. Then she ran back to the big kids, and Pranav walked home, lighter.

qa.q: Where did Papa find Pranav?
qa.a: Papa found Pranav sitting by the well, throwing pebbles.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling on the walk home?
qa.a: He felt lighter and happier, glad he'd tried even though Elizabeth went back to the big kids.

qa.q: What did Papa do that helped Pranav?
qa.a: He listened, suggested one small invitation, and helped Pranav see that the old friendship was real even if things change.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth feel when Pranav invites her?
qa.a: Elizabeth may feel a bit surprised and pleased to be remembered, which is why she agreed to a game.

grounding: A parent helps a child say hello and invite an old friend to one game, accepting that friendships change with seasons.
